title: Clarify billing semantics for server-initiated retrievals and mid-request tool chains
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Server-side components invoked as part of a single API call (retrieval services, toolchains, rerankers, external function calls) can consume untracked or misattributed tokens. Examples: a model asks the retrieval service mid-generation which issues new model calls; a toolchain fan-out kicks off reranker calls; a server-side plugin prefetches context. These additional tokens can be charged to the wrong tenant, counted twice, or never credited/refunded when flows abort. This ticket defines consistent billing attribution semantics and implements the minimal runtime and ledger changes to guarantee correct per-request accounting for server-initiated mid-request work.

Goals:
- Always charge token consumption caused by work initiated on behalf of a customer API request to that customer's account (API key) unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- Provide a compact provenance chain so post-hoc audits can map tokens to the originating request and to intermediate components.
- Handle streaming edge cases (midstream tool calls, retries, reconnects, aborts) so final charges are deterministic and idempotent.
- Enable retrocrediting for speculative prefetches or aborted fan-outs when we detect no customer-visible benefit.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens consumed by server-initiated retrievals/tool-calls are recorded with an origin_provenance_id linking back to the parent API request
Accounting ledger can attribute every token to exactly one charge event for completed requests and produce provisional entries for in-flight work
Shadow billing run (7 days) shows <0.1% delta between old and new attribution for typical workloads except when previous misattribution existed (documented)
Race conditions: reconnects/retries must not create duplicate charges for the same logical work (idempotency test pass)
Retrocredit flow exists: when speculative mid-request work did not contribute to final output (server-determined), system issues a rollback/credit within SLA window
technical_decisions: Introduce origin_provenance_id (UUID) propagated with every internal call triggered by an API request; runtime will attach this to token ledger entries
Ledger schema extension: add flat fields 'provenance_id' and 'origin_kind' with allowed values user_input|server_tool|retrieval|reranker|cache_hit
Propagate lightweight headers (X-RW-Provenance: <id>|<role>) across services; enforce in RPC gateway and runtime shim
Speculative prefetches default to 'provisional' ledger entries that are finalized or rolled back by finalization hooks; provisional entries are not invoiced until finalized

Backwards-compatible: if downstream service doesn't support provenance headers, runtime will mark entries with origin_kind=server_tool_unattributed and surface these to billing reports for remediation

Streaming semantics: when a model triggers a tool call mid-stream, the tool-invocation receives the parent's provenance_id and returns token usage; runtime treats tool tokens as part of the parent stream's finalization boundary
Idempotency keys: attach idempotency_token to fan-out work so retries or duplicate RPCs share ledger entries rather than creating new ones

Cross-tenant cache reuse: cache hits by other tenants are charged to the original requestor only if cache contract indicates tenant-scoped entry; otherwise cache warmup costs are considered infrastructure expense (configurable per cache)
test_plan: Unit tests: provenance header propagation across service mocks, ledger entry creation with provenance_id
Integration: e2e test where a generation triggers a retrieval which itself triggers a reranker; assert final ledger rows map to root provenance_id
Fuzz: simulate midstream aborts, reconnects, and duplicate RPCs to validate idempotency keys prevent double-charges
Shadow billing: run actual traffic through new attribution pipeline for 7 days and compare totals to production billing; produce variance report
Audit tests: replay recorded traces and verify final invoice matches per-trace attribution within tolerance
Performance: measure additional latency and storage overhead for provenance fields under p95 traffic (target <1% latency increase)
Compliance: ensure provenance headers do not leak PII and are redacted in logs as required
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (instrument-only): propagate provenance_id but write entries to 'shadow_ledger' (no billing) for 2 weeks
Phase 1 (shadow billing): compute invoices with new attribution in parallel; compare and hold actual invoices on old pipeline; run customer-facing reconciliation for 7 days
Phase 2 (soft enforce): enable provisional-finalize flow for new requests; still use old pipeline for legacy in-flight sessions; open a 14-day rollback window for posts
Phase 3 (enforce): switch billing pipeline to use new ledger entries; run retrocredit script for identified speculative overcharges older than 24h but within SLA window
Monitoring: dashboards for provisional vs finalized tokens, unattributed entries, and retrocredit volume; automated alerts when unattributed >0.05% of token volume
